modelResponse.episodeSummary: Aisha N. Rahman, 34F, Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (PSVT), warning, hemodynamically stable
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Narrow QRS, no clear P waves, abrupt onset
modelResponse.primaryEtiology: Re-entrant circuit involving AV node (AVNRT) or accessory pathway (AVRT)
modelResponse.mechanism: Increased automaticity or triggered activity within the AV node or accessory pathway leading to a re-entrant circuit.

rejectedAlternatives.why: Rhythm is regular, not irregularly irregular.
Rhythm is regular with a 1:1 AV conduction (atrial rate = ventricular rate), no clear flutter waves described.
No clear P waves preceding each QRS complex; rate is very high for sinus tachycardia in this context.
QRS duration is narrow (88ms), not wide (>120ms).

recommendedActions: Administer IV adenosine 6 mg rapid push (standard first-line therapy for stable SVT)
If adenosine ineffective, consider IV calcium channel blocker (e.g., diltiazem) or beta-blocker (e.g., metoprolol) - use cautiously given potential for hypotension
If rhythm converts, consider admission for observation and further workup
If rhythm persists or patient becomes unstable, prepare for synchronized cardioversion
uncertainty: Specific type of PSVT (AVNRT vs AVRT) cannot be definitively determined from ECG alone.
No information on prior treatments for SVT episodes.
